epic.title: Virtual Office Foundation
epic.objective: Establish the Phaser-based virtual-office presentation inside the existing Electron/React desktop application using one fixed 2D pixel-art room, a small original asset set created for Coffee Break, three animated mock agents, and read-only agent inspection.
design: One fixed office room with recognizable work and coffee-break areas.
Three mock agents visible simultaneously: one idle, one working, and one on break.
Subtle, state-specific looping animations; no autonomous navigation.
No live AI-provider or Connector integration.
exit_criteria: The desktop application renders the office room and all three mock agents.
Idle, working, and break states are visually distinguishable.
The office remains usable at supported desktop window sizes.
Relevant automated, visual, and interaction checks pass.

stories.title: Integrate Phaser Office Scene
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to see a Phaser-powered office scene inside Coffee Break so that the desktop application can display the virtual workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Phaser mounts within a designated area of the existing React desktop interface.
A locally rendered placeholder room is visible when the desktop application launches.
Phaser initialization and disposal follow the React host lifecycle.
Ordinary React remounting leaves no duplicate canvases, game instances, or listeners.
The integration preserves Electron security boundaries and does not access providers directly.
Relevant typecheck, lint, test, and build checks pass; a local desktop launch confirms scene rendering.
stories.boundary: Integration and lifecycle only. No finished office art, agents, selection panel, or dedicated resizing behavior.

stories.title: Build the Pixel-Art Office
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a recognizable pixel-art office so that I can distinguish the agents’ work and break areas.
acceptance_criteria: One fixed room contains recognizable work and coffee-break areas.
The room uses a small, original pixel-art asset set created specifically for Coffee Break.
Desks, coffee station, flooring, and other necessary elements follow a consistent pixel scale and visual style.
The room defines three unobstructed agent positions appropriate to the planned mock states.
Assets are bundled locally and require no runtime downloads.
A desktop screenshot and visual review confirm that the room and agent positions are readable.
stories.boundary: Fixed environment and room art only. No furniture editor, multiple rooms, agent movement, or finished character sprites.

stories.title: Render Animated Mock Agents
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to see three animated agents with distinct states so that I can understand their simulated activity at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: Three agents render simultaneously from typed, deterministic mock data.
Their initial states are idle, working, and break, with one agent in each state.
Each agent has a stable identity, display name, state, and mock activity description.
A small, original pixel-art character asset set supports subtle, looping, state-specific animations.
State distinctions do not rely on color alone.
Agents occupy designated positions without obscuring essential room elements.
Rendering is data-driven rather than three unrelated hard-coded character implementations.
Mock states are clearly simulated and do not imply live provider activity.
stories.boundary: Visual states and looping animations only. No autonomous navigation, real-time provider events, task execution, or simulation engine.

stories.title: Inspect an Agent
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to select an agent and inspect its details so that I can understand who it represents and what it is doing.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking an agent selects it and displays a visible selection indicator.
The React interface displays the selected agent’s name, current state, and mock activity.
Selecting another agent updates the details without retaining stale information.
A defined interaction clears the selection.
Displayed details remain consistent with typed mock data.
An accessible keyboard-operated mechanism supports selecting agents and inspecting their details.
The interaction issues no agent commands and does not communicate with external providers.
stories.boundary: Read-only inspection. No agent control, chat, task history, or live activity feed.

stories.title: Support Office Resizing
stories.user_story: As a user, I want the office to remain usable when I resize the desktop window so that I can continue viewing and inspecting agents.
acceptance_criteria: Resizing creates no duplicate Phaser instances, canvases, or listeners.
Pixel-art rendering remains visually consistent without unintended smoothing or distortion.
The room and all three agents remain accessible at the supported minimum desktop window size.
Selected-agent details remain accessible at that size.
Selection targets remain aligned with rendered agents after resizing.
Repeated resizing does not break selection or leave stale scene elements.
Verification covers the normal desktop size and a documented minimum supported size.
stories.boundary: Desktop-window resizing only. No mobile layout, alternate room configuration, or zoom-control feature.

stories.title: Verify the Virtual Office MVP
stories.user_story: As a developer, I want to verify the integrated virtual office so that its rendering, mock states, interactions, and lifecycle behavior remain reliable.
acceptance_criteria: The integrated desktop application launches and displays the completed office.
Verification confirms all three mock agents render in their intended initial states.
Verification covers selecting an agent, switching selection, and clearing selection.
Verification covers relevant mounting, unmounting, and resizing behavior.
Automated tests cover appropriate deterministic logic and interaction boundaries without unnecessarily duplicating existing tests.
Desktop visual and accessibility checks are documented, including limitations.
Typecheck, lint, tests, and build pass.
An independent review confirms the integrated experience meets EP-02 exit criteria.
stories.boundary: Integration verification and necessary corrections only. No new office features or live Connector integration.
